text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

Both you and the successful candidate are men, so sex cannot easily explain why he was preferred over you. An all-male panel may say something about the department's recruitment culture, or breach rules on balanced panels in some jurisdictions — but it is not evidence of bias against you. Raising it would likely read as a scattershot grievance and weaken your credibility.

Your real argument is much stronger: you appear objectively better qualified on the stated criteria (completed PhD, six papers, four years teaching), and "industry experience" needs to have been a published, weighted criterion — not introduced afterwards.

Send a written follow-up citing your right to a reasoned decision, note the two-week silence, and ask for the panel's scoring against the advertised criteria.
